newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: A 25-basis point official rate cut on Friday was not enough to support Spain's debt market, which fell under fears that the U.S. Federal reserve could hike its own key rate, dealers said.
"The market is getting very nervous for a possible rate hike in the States," a dealer here said.
A falling peseta, despite apparent buying by the Bank of Spain, also added pressure to a market still worried by a possible EMU delay, dealers added.
Chart analysts put strong support at 111.70/80 for long-term futures. "If it breaks that level, it could go to 111."
The 10-year cash spread over Bunds widened to 132 bps from 129 bps earlier this morning, and the yield curve flattened again.
Earlier this morning, the Bank of Spain sanctioned its second rate cut of the year, pushing its key money rate to 5.75 pct.
Though largely expected, the move was considered a bit too hasty by a few dealers, who said both financial markets and the peseta could suffer.
